top_stories.title: OpenAI reportedly disbanded its preparedness team
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has dissolved its preparedness team, which was responsible for evaluating risks from its most powerful AI models. The move raises questions about the company's ongoing commitment to AI safety as it continues to ship new products at pace. The Verge reports the team's responsibilities may have been folded into other parts of the organisation.

top_stories.title: Stripe Clinches over $7B Deal to Buy AI Firm OpenRouter [Paywalled]
top_stories.summary: Stripe has agreed to acquire OpenRouter, a platform that acts as a unified API gateway for accessing large language models from multiple AI providers, for over $7 billion. The deal signals major consolidation in the AI infrastructure layer and gives Stripe a significant foothold in the AI developer tooling market. OpenRouter has become a key intermediary for businesses routing AI compute across providers.

top_stories.title: ChatGPT's Computer History tracks your clicks and keystrokes
top_stories.summary: OpenAI's ChatGPT now logs detailed computer activity including clicks and keystrokes as part of its computer use history feature. The Verge reports this raises significant user privacy concerns about the scope of data being captured during AI-assisted computer interactions. The feature is part of OpenAI's broader push into AI personal assistant capabilities.

top_stories.title: Rogue AI aren't science fiction anymore
top_stories.summary: The Verge examines how the concept of rogue or misaligned AI systems, long confined to science fiction, is increasingly being treated as a near-term practical concern by researchers and policymakers. The piece explores how recent AI capabilities are forcing a reassessment of safety frameworks and what constitutes acceptable AI behaviour. It draws on current industry developments to argue that these risks now demand serious, concrete responses.

top_stories.title: AI isn't outthinking mathematicians, it's out-remembering them
top_stories.summary: A detailed analysis argues that recent AI breakthroughs in mathematics are better explained by vast memorisation of existing proofs and patterns rather than genuine novel reasoning or discovery. The piece contends that framing AI performance on mathematical benchmarks as 'outthinking' human experts is misleading and obscures important limitations in current large language models. The distinction has significant implications for how AI capabilities are evaluated and communicated.

further_links.title: Young People Hate AI CEOs So Passionately That It's Almost Hard to Believe
further_links.summary: A new poll finds that young people hold strongly negative views of AI company executives, reflecting broader tensions between public sentiment and the AI industry's rapid growth.

further_links.title: AI Coding Without the Vibes
further_links.summary: A practical guide arguing for a more disciplined, structured approach to using AI coding tools rather than relying on ad hoc prompting, with concrete techniques for getting reliable results.

further_links.title: The AI Credit Resale Economy
further_links.summary: An examination of the emerging ecosystem of token brokers who buy and resell AI compute credits, acting as intermediaries between AI providers and end users at scale.

further_links.title: AI-Assisted GPU Porting of a 250k Line Legacy Weather Simulation Code
further_links.summary: Researchers used AI tools to assist in porting a large legacy scientific codebase to GPU architecture, offering insights into AI's practical role in large-scale software engineering tasks.

further_links.title: From Rule-Based Automation to AI Agents: The Future of Enterprise Applications
further_links.summary: An overview of how enterprise software is transitioning from traditional rule-based automation to AI agent frameworks, with implications for business operations and software vendors.

further_links.title: Cloudflare's AI Psychosis
further_links.summary: A critical look at how Cloudflare's AI-powered security systems are generating erratic and counterproductive behaviour, raising concerns about reliability and unintended consequences of deploying AI at infrastructure scale.

further_links.title: Have a laugh at AI's expense by roleplaying as a chatbot
further_links.summary: The Verge highlights a growing trend of users roleplaying as AI chatbots, using the format to satirise and expose the quirks and limitations of current AI systems.

further_links.title: These 'Masturbation Consultants' Were Hired to Pleasure Themselves With AI [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports on a niche but growing category of AI product testing, where companies hire consultants to evaluate AI-driven adult content and intimacy tools, raising questions about labour, consent, and technology ethics.
